name: cruise
description: Cruise control for Claude Code: watches the context, shows where you are and (optionally) picks the reasoning effort for each prompt

context.title: Context warnings
context.description: Warn when the context fills up and point to /handoff.

warnAt.title: First warning (% of context)
warnAt.description: Context percentage that triggers the first, gentle warning.

urgentAt.title: Urgent warning (% of context)
urgentAt.description: Context percentage that triggers the urgent warning and a system notification. Never below the first warning.

resetBelow.title: Reset below (% of context)
resetBelow.description: After a compaction drops the context below this percentage, warnings start over. Never above the first warning.

contextAction.title: When the context fills
contextAction.description: button: a row above the prompt offers a button that does the handoff, clears the conversation and continues (the default). alert: only the warnings. auto: at the automatic point it does all three by itself between turns; it CLEARS your conversation, so turn it on only if you want that.

autoAt.title: Automatic handoff at (%)
autoAt.description: Only for contextAction auto: the percent of context at which Cruise saves the handoff, clears the conversation and picks up by itself. 80 (the same as the urgent warning) leaves room for the handoff itself; lower is safer for long answers. Kept between the first warning and 95.

purser.title: Purser mode
purser.description: A standing instruction so Claude's replies are easy to act on and cheap to read, like a cabin crew's announcements: result or next action first, numbered steps, one Now/Done/Next line on multi-step work, no preamble or recap. Adds about 500 tokens to the cached system prompt. Turn it off to keep Claude's default style.

minAskChars.title: Minimum request length
minAskChars.description: Messages shorter than this many characters (such as "go ahead") do not replace the request shown in the band.

effort.title: Effort steering
effort.description: Pick the reasoning effort for each prompt with a small judge: off, haiku (your own Claude login, no key, the default), jev (TypeSafe hosted API, needs a key) or laya (a model running on your machine, see the README). Run /cruise to see what it is choosing.

steer.title: Steering direction
steer.description: both: the judge may raise or lower the effort from the one set in your app. down: it may only lower it.

topLevel.title: Highest effort the judge may pick
topLevel.description: The highest effort the judge may pick when a job is hard: high, xhigh or max (every level your model offers; xhigh is the default; Anthropic suggests max only where it shows a gain). Lower it if you want a cheaper ceiling.

routerModels.title: Router models to steer (opt-in)
routerModels.description: Off by default (empty). Only for people who run Claude Code through a router such as claude-code-router: comma-separated patterns, * is the wildcard, exact case, of the models whose effort Cruise may steer too, for example OpenAI (Login)/gpt-*,Google (Login)/gemini-*. Measured through one gateway: changing the effort cost GPT the whole prompt cache and Gemini part of it, and the same Anthropic model lost its cache too, so Anthropic ids behind a router are left alone unless you name them here. The judge's levels pass through unchanged, because the router maps them; on GPT, max costs far more tokens than high, so consider topLevel high. Behind a router the Haiku judge is not used until judgeModel names a model your router serves. Plain Claude Code is not affected either way.

judgeUrl.title: Judge URL (jev or laya)
judgeUrl.description: Where the judge listens. Empty uses https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone for jev and http://127.0.0.1:18787/v1/systemone for laya.

judgeKey.title: Judge key (jev)
judgeKey.description: TypeSafe API key for jev. A laya server on your own machine needs none. Kept in Claude Code's secure storage.

judgeModel.title: Judge model
judgeModel.description: The model that judges each prompt. Haiku judge: empty means claude-haiku-5-5; behind a router (such as claude-code-router) the Haiku judge is not used until you name a model your router serves here, for example Google (Login)/gemini-3.5-flash-lite. Jev or Laya: which checkpoint to ask for (empty lets the server choose: Jev jev-latest, Laya routes by language; use it to point Laya at a checkpoint you trained).

updates.title: Update check
updates.description: check: look on GitHub once a day and tell you when a new version exists. Never installs automatically; you decide when to install (/cruise:update). off: never check.
